en: A downstream repository, OSCILLA, audited on 2026-10-04 against v0.13.0 (e08aec8651), shows the tool breaking its adopters in ways no test in this repository sees, because every test here runs this repository's own layout. Installing 0.12.0 machine-wide made doctor report <n1/> failures in OSCILLA: unsealed plan stamps and use-case steps reclassified as state-mutating. Its pre-commit hook runs doctor, so every commit was refused until the layer was migrated by hand, and the migrated layer is then rejected by <n2/>. Nothing records which tool version a layer was written for, and migrate handles only .majordomus to .ai. Live use-case scenarios refuse read-only knowledge subcommands while admitting check --checkpoint, which writes. Upgrading the vendored rules leaves the policy and source keys they depend on behind. The knowledge deriver writes untracked candidates onto a trunk that only pull requests change. The vendored rules and the init skeleton carry this repository's narrative, test paths and stack.

Instalace 0.12.0 pro celý stroj způsobila, že doctor hlásil v OSCILLA <n1/> selhání: nezapečetěná razítka plánu a kroky případů užití překlasifikované jako měnící stav. Jeho pre-commit hook spouští doctor, takže každý commit byl odmítnut, dokud se vrstva ručně nemigrovala, a migrovaná vrstva je pak odmítnuta verzí <n2/>. Živé scénáře případů užití odmítají podpříkazy znalostí jen pro čtení, zatímco připouštějí check --checkpoint, který zapisuje. The record is written and its `task_id` is `none`, which is a fact a later reader can place; the ledger event it emits carries no `task_id` at all, because every reader of that event collects the field's distinct values as task identifiers. This scenario expected exit <n1/> until ADR <n2/>: refusing here meant that finishing a task silenced progress records for every episode after it, which is exactly what happened to this repository for six days from 2026-09-05.
cs: Checkpoint patří epizodě, ne úloze. Žádná plocha nespouští jiný program, aby získala vývojovou sémantiku: plocha, která volá shell, vlastní sestavení argumentů, interpretaci návratových kódů a vykreslení chyb, což jsou sémantika, ať jsou napsány kdekoli.

en: <t1/> <t2>One issue with the branches that name it — local, and remote-tracking where only the remote still has the branch — and, for each, the commits it holds that the trunk did not: measured against the trunk while the branch is open, and against the first parent of the merge commit that brought it in once it is merged. A branch that reached the trunk without a merge commit of its own says so and claims nothing, because its commits cannot be told from the trunk's. The milestone comes from the canonical issue record, which is the one edge here that git does not hold, and `declared` says whether the project model has this id at all — a repository with no plan still gets the branches, and a typo still cannot read as work nobody did.</t2> <t3> <t4>query</t4> <t5>behaviorally_verified</t5> <t6>mcp</t6> <t7>http</t7> </t3>
